correctness.rationale: For the stated quadratic family, Adaptive Gradient Clipping is locally inactive by a strict source-threshold inequality and Gradient Centralization leaves exactly \(\delta q\). Zero moment initialization then gives \(\widehat v_1=\delta^2(q\odot q)\), so the published stable-decay scale is exactly proportional to \(1/|\delta|\). The adaptive update remains bounded because its denominator includes \(\epsilon>0\). The package replay checks the concrete source-default clipping witness and the inverse-distance law.

The original Stable Weight Decay source retains an epsilon safeguard, and later first-party code also protects this denominator, but neither inspected source states the strongly convex singular family or the exact inverse-distance blow-up. value.rationale: Ranger21 is explicitly motivated by composing individually useful optimizer modules, so cross-component well-definedness is structurally central rather than cosmetic. The obstruction occurs on a smooth strongly convex quadratic and extends from an exact undefined state to an unbounded \(1/|\delta|\) neighborhood. It also identifies why a safeguard present in the original Stable Weight Decay rule and later implementation is mathematically necessary in the published composition.
